name: file.wait
description: Block until at least one path matching `glob` appears on the filesystem, or `timeout_ms` expires. Returns the first matched path. Tolerates files and directories.

glob.description: File-system glob pattern (e.g. `C:\Users\Admin\Downloads\*.pdf`). Wildcards: `*` (any chars in a single path component), `?` (single char). No recursive `**` glob — use a fixed-depth pattern or watch.file for recursive scenarios.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait in milliseconds. Returns ERR timeout if no match appears within this window. Default 30 seconds.

path.description: First path that matched the glob. When multiple match simultaneously, the agent picks one (typically lexicographically first); callers needing all matches should follow up with directory.list.

x-implementations.name: read_directory_changes_w
x-implementations.description: Win32 `ReadDirectoryChangesW` on the parent directory of the glob's literal prefix; agent filters incoming notifications against the glob pattern. Available NT 5+. Falls back to FindFirstChangeNotification on NT 4 / 9x (less precise — returns directory-changed event without per-file detail; agent must re-scan the directory).

windows-modern.description: ReadDirectoryChangesW on the glob's parent directory. Initial scan covers the case where a matching path already exists at call time. ERR not_found if the parent directory doesn't exist (the wait can't begin).

windows-classic.description: ReadDirectoryChangesW on NT 5+ (XP onwards); FindFirstChangeNotification + re-scan loop on NT 4 / 9x. The fallback path is less efficient (it polls the directory after each change notification) but functionally equivalent.
